a9ee651 fix: correctly extract markdown with nested code blocks in designs [90m(21/01/2026)[0m
  CRITICAL BUG FIX: The extractMarkdown function was using a non-greedy
  regex that stopped at the FIRST closing ``` it found, even if that was
  inside a nested code block. This caused design content to be truncated
  mid-sentence when the design included code examples.
  
  Example of bug:
  ```markdown
  # UI Placement
  
  Place the form between:
  
  ```jsx          <-- Regex stopped here!
  <Component />
  ```
  
  Rest lost...    <-- Everything after was cut off
  ```
  
  Root cause:
  - Regex: /```markdown\s*([\s\S]*?)\s*```/
  - The ([\s\S]*?) is non-greedy and matches minimally
  - Stops at first ``` (even inside nested code blocks)
  
  Solution:
  - Parse fence markers properly by position (line start check)
  - Count depth of nested code blocks (opening vs closing)
  - Only close when depth returns to 0
  - Handle edge case where closing fence is missing
  
  Testing:
  - Created test with nested ```jsx...``` block
  - Old code: extracted only 70 chars (cut after "section:")
  - New code: extracted all 348 chars correctly
  
  This fixes GitHub issue #15 and any other instances where designs
  with code examples were being truncated.
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

  pages/api/ instead of src/pages/api/. This caused Next.js to ignore
  the entire src/pages/ directory (including the home page), resulting
  in 404 errors on all routes.
  
  In Next.js, when both pages/ and src/pages/ exist, Next.js uses pages/
  and ignores src/pages/. Since pages/ only contained the API endpoint,
  the home page and all other routes were not built.
  
  Changes:
  - Moved pages/api/test-telegram.ts → src/pages/api/test-telegram.ts
  - Removed empty pages/ directory
  
  This restores the home page and all other routes.
  
  Issue started in commit: 8a32e98
  Symptoms: 404 on home page in production
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

1288e9c refactor: use Vercel's automatic VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL [90m(21/01/2026)[0m
  Updated getBaseUrl() to prioritize Vercel's automatic stable production
  URL (VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL) instead of manually setting
  NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL.
  
  Changes:
  - Updated getBaseUrl() priority order:
    1. VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL (automatic stable domain)
    2. VERCEL_URL (deployment-specific)
    3. NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (optional manual override)
    4. localhost:3000 (local dev)
  
  - Updated documentation to clarify NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is optional
  - Added explanation of Vercel's automatic URL variables to .env.example
  - Marked NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL as optional in init guide
  
  Why this is better:
  - Vercel automatically provides stable production URL
  - No manual configuration needed for *.vercel.app domains
  - NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL only needed for custom domains
  - Reduces setup complexity
  
  Sources:
  - https://vercel.com/docs/environment-variables/system-environment-variables
  - https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/16429
  
  Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
